title: skills(objectstack-data): a `user` field's declared `deleteBehavior` now takes effect when the user is deleted (#29253) — the field-type and relationship rules should say so
body:
domain:server#5 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQKwKFCp1m6Pb6Q8c1

Source: PR #29368 (#29253), the `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` line.

From #29253 (`fix(objectql)!`, a narrowing): a `user` field that declares `deleteBehavior` joins the referential delete walk when the user is deleted, and reads it as a `lookup` reads its own. `cascade` deletes the rows holding the user. `set_null` clears the field, and a `multiple: true` field loses only that member. `restrict` refuses the delete with `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED`. A `user` field with no `deleteBehavior` stays out of the walk, as before.

Ask: the skill text teaches this.
- `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md`: the `user` row lists `deleteBehavior` as an option with the behaviour above.
- `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md`: the delete-behaviour section names `user` among the reference types the walk reads, only when the field declares a behaviour.
The docs page `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx` is already updated in #29368. Lands after #29368 merges. This is a governed surface, so the PR lands by approval.
